subject: QBR Prep: Launch Velocity Inventory & Risk Playbook
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 24 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: QBR Prep: Launch Velocity Inventory & Risk Playbook

Team —

QBR is two weeks out; I need a consolidated view we can present to execs that answers three things succinctly for each launch line:

1) Launch velocity status (on-track / at-risk / blocked) and delta to original timeline.
2) Top 3 delivery risks with severity, owner, and target mitigation date.
3) Recommended go/no-go gating (metrics or conditions we must meet).

Please update the attached launch_risks_tracker.xlsx and drop a one-line summary in reply by EOD Tuesday 26 Jan. Also attach any short artifacts (benchmarks, infra tickets) you want included. I will synthesize into the QBR slide deck and run a dry-run with product + CS on Thursday.

Immediate notes from me: the new 2-stage canary is going into integration this week — if infra visibility or throughput regressions pop, we need an alternative rollback plan to avoid blocking a customer-facing launch. Marcus: please surface latency/throughput variance and whether model quantization changes alter rollout gates. Laura: highlight any external dependency (partner APIs, feature flags) that could shift date. Steph: note readiness for canary monitoring and alert thresholds.

Attachments: launch_risks_tracker.xlsx, roadmap_timeline_v2.pdf

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR Prep: Launch Velocity Inventory & Risk Playbook

Hannah —

One-line status for the models team: AT-RISK (medium). Delta: +10 business days vs. baseline due to kernel tuning and additional test vectors.

Top risks (brief):
- Throughput variance after quantization (severity: high) — owner: marcus_lin — mitigation: complete kernel A/B by 27 Jan; fallback: use FP16 without quantization for first canary (target 27 Jan).
- KV-cache eviction under tail latencies (severity: medium) — owner: infra (cc Vivek) — mitigation: increase cache memory and add suffix-based cache warmers (target 02 Feb).
- Model size / packaging regressions for Dedicated images (severity: low) — owner: infra build team — mitigation: enforce strict container size checks in CI (target 29 Jan).

Attached a quick throughput snapshot and an internal note on variance (throughput-benchmark.pdf). Short ask: if product expects the canary to hit 100 RPS sustained we should either delay by 10 days or reduce canary volume to 30% for the initial rollout.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Engineering Manager, Model Serving
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 15:26:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR Prep: Launch Velocity Inventory & Risk Playbook

Hannah / Marcus —

Thanks Marcus — a couple of points from Product side:
- External dependency: Acme Corp has a nonstandard session-mapping API. If their shim isn't stable by last integration test (02 Feb) we should treat the Acme launch as BLOCKED until partner provides a hotfix. Owner: Acme integration (we have weekly sync with them).
- Gating proposal: for customer-facing launches we require 95th p95 latency within X ms of current GA, and no more than 1.5x error budget burn during canary window. If Marcus's throughput tests indicate we can't meet those thresholds, we should adopt the reduced-volume canary Marcus suggested.

I updated the roadmap_timeline_v2.pdf with minor date shifts and annotated the Acme dependency (see attached). For the QBR slides I want the team to be ready to commit to either: (A) a soft launch with constrained usage and explicit partner caveats, or (B) delay 2 weeks and keep full volume. We need a recommended option.

Laura Bennett
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 26 Jan 2027 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR Prep: Launch Velocity Inventory & Risk Playbook

Team —

Operational mitigation summary from Observability/OPS:
- Canary plan: Stage 1 (30% traffic, 1 hour ramp, auto-rollforward disabled). Stage 2 (60% traffic, 6 hour ramp) only if error budget burn < 0.3% and p95 latency within threshold.
- Alerts / thresholds: p95 latency > baseline + 20% -> page infra and models. Error rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m -> rollback.
- Dashboards: I will create a dedicated QBR canary dashboard and link it in the drive folder by EOD Wednesday.

Risks I see: insufficient log sampling for tail-latency debugging (medium). Mitigation: increase tail-sampling by 4x in canary window (will coordinate with infra, Vivek).

Attaching the short runbook stub for emergency rollback (no binary, just runbook reference). I agree with Laura: present two options (soft constrained launch vs delay). Ops prefers soft-constrained if Product accepts the reduced SLA for the first week.

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: QBR Prep: Launch Velocity Inventory & Risk Playbook

Thanks all — this is exactly what we need. Quick synthesis and action items for exec slide: 

- Synthesis: Primary launches are "At-Risk (medium)" due to throughput variance from quantization and an external partner dependency (Acme). Proposed path: proceed with a constrained-volume canary (30%) for initial rollout, with automated rollback thresholds and a 2-week parallel remediation track for throughput fixes.

Action items (owners / dates):
- Marcus: finalize kernel A/B and confirm FP16 fallback plan (complete by 2027-01-27) — if metrics still fail, prepare reduced-volume canary config.
- Vivek: increase KV-cache memory and coordinate tail-sampling change with Ops (complete by 2027-02-02).
- Laura: confirm Acme partner readiness and sign-off on constrained launch option (update by 2027-02-01).
- Stephanie: publish QBR canary dashboard and runbook; validate alert thresholds in staging (complete by 2027-01-28).

I'll incorporate this into the QBR deck and schedule a 30-minute dry run with Exec and CS Friday 29 Jan at 10:00 AM PT — calendar invite to follow. If anyone thinks the synthesis misrepresents their risk severity, call it out in a reply and I'll adjust.

Attachments included in thread: launch_risks_tracker.xlsx, roadmap_timeline_v2.pdf, throughput-benchmark.pdf

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
